OmaStats 1.9.1 narrows two things the plugin does on your behalf: the Allow TRIM fix now trims only the volume it names, and the public-IP lookup no longer follows redirects.

[Download the complete plugin](https://github.com/crmne/omastats/releases/download/v1.9.1/omastats-v1.9.1.tar.gz), or install it with:

```sh
omarchy plugin add https://github.com/crmne/omastats.git --enable
```

## Fixed

- **Allow TRIM trims only the volume it names.** After letting TRIM through an encrypted volume, the fix ran `sudo fstrim -av`, which trims every mounted filesystem, although its prompt named one volume. It now says before asking that it will trim that volume's mount point, and runs `fstrim -v` on it alone. A volume whose mount point has spaces or other unusual characters is not trimmed right away; the weekly timer or a manual `fstrim` covers it. By @crmne, from the marketplace security review.
- **The public-IP lookup follows no redirects.** The Python sampler let urllib follow a redirect, which reads the whole redirect body before the 65-byte cap applied, and could send the lookup to a host other than the three listed ones. It now refuses redirects and reads only a successful answer. The native sampler's `curl` call already followed none, but could take a redirect's body as the answer; it now accepts only a successful answer and stops reading past 64 bytes. By @crmne, from the marketplace security review.

## Known limitations

- Peripheral battery levels and charging states can be up to ten minutes old.
- Mac fans come from the SMC's ACPI device, where T2 Macs publish them. This was tested on a MacBookPro16,1 only.
- The bar places each readout on whole logical pixels, so at some scales a readout can still sit up to about a device pixel off the bar's centre.
- A laptop's NVIDIA card is read once per idle period (about six seconds) while it is allowed to suspend, so its figures update less often than the rest. This was checked with tests, not on a hybrid laptop: please report how it behaves on yours.
- Without a power supply, battery or platform zone to measure the whole machine, the Power total covers the CPU and GPUs only, not fans, drives or the rest of the board.
- CPU power and its RAPL zones on Intel, and on AMD without integrated graphics, need a udev rule that makes `/sys/class/powercap/*/energy_uj` readable.
- Power supply readings cover Corsair's USB-connected supplies (the `corsairpsu` driver) only.
- NVIDIA fans report percent of full speed, not rpm, so they do not count towards the Fans ring's average.
- The process search and color fields take typed text only: there is no paste or text selection.
- GPU process lists from open drivers show only your own processes. An integrated AMD card's own load figure jumps between 0% and 100%, so it can disagree with its process list.
- A mirror, raidz or striped ZFS pool counts against its first data drive only. "All disks" is correct, but picking another drive in the pool shows no space for it.
- A vertical bar with many readouts turned on can run into the bar's center section. Turn off readouts you don't need, or use figure-only looks.

## Thanks

Thanks to HANCORE-linux for the marketplace security review that found both.

Both bundled binaries are rebuilt twice in CI, compared byte-for-byte with the committed executables, and covered by checksums and GitHub build attestations.
